chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who made a mistake behind the Imam after the opening of the prayer; he did not say anything, did not say Takbir, did not say Subhanallah, and did not recite the Tashahhud until he gave the Taslim. He said: 'His prayer is valid, and he is not required to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdat al-Sahw) if he makes a mistake behind the Imam, because the Imam is responsible for the prayer of those behind him.'

key_terms.افْتَتَحَ الصَّلَاةَ: The opening of the prayer (typically referring to Takbirat al-Ihram)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ ضَامِنٌ: The Imam is responsible/guarantor (for the validity of the followers' prayer)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: The two prostrations of forgetfulness performed to compensate for minor errors in prayer
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدْ: Reciting the Tashahhud (testimony and blessings upon the Prophet)
key_terms.يُسَلِّمَ: To conclude the prayer with the Taslim (salutation)

ai.seo_question: Is a worshipper required to perform Sajdat al-Sahw if they make a mistake behind the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential principle that a follower (*ma'mum*) is exempt from *Sajdat al-Sahw* when praying behind an Imam, as the Imam's validity guarantees the follower's prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the Imam's role as the guarantor of congregational prayer, distinguishing it from individual prayer where forgetfulness requires specific corrective prostrations. The hadith underscores the communal nature of Salah, where the leader's actions serve as a sufficient cover for the followers' minor errors.
